text: True or False: Skolem's paradox shows that ZFC is actually inconsistent, because ZFC proves uncountable sets exist yet (by downward Löwenheim–Skolem) has a countable model.
explanation: False. Skolem's paradox is not a contradiction: 'uncountable' is relative to a model. A countable model of ZFC contains a set it internally believes is uncountable because the model lacks the bijection with ω that an outside observer can see. No inconsistency follows — the paradox only shows countability is model-relative.
